create_note.description: Add a note to a contact, company or deal. Choose at least one, or the note won't show up anywhere in HubSpot. A contact can be named by email address, and so can several at once (everyone from outside on a call), with no step to find them first.

create_note.name: create_note

parameters.description: The note's text.
parameters.name: body

parameters.description: Contact to attach the note to.
parameters.name: contact_id

parameters.description: Attach the note to the contact with this email address, when you have their email but not the contact. The step fails when nobody in HubSpot has it, unless Add the contact if new is on. Ignored when a contact is chosen above. Beta: it can also hold several addresses, as a list from an earlier step (a Gong call's customer_emails) or as text with commas between them, such as sam@customer.com, kim@customer.com. Then it goes on every one of them that is a HubSpot contact and the others are skipped; what happens when none of them is a contact is set by If no contact is found.
parameters.name: contact_email

parameters.description: Beta. With Contact's email: what to do when nobody in HubSpot has the address, or any of the addresses. fail stops the workflow with an error, as it always has. skip creates no note and carries on, with created false in the result. Leave empty for fail.

options.label: Skip: create no note and carry on

parameters.description: Beta. With Contact's email: when nobody in HubSpot has that address yet (a first-time payer or booker), add them as a contact and attach the note to them instead of failing. An existing contact is left as it is.

parameters.description: Company to attach the note to.
parameters.name: company_id

parameters.description: Deal to attach the note to.

created.description: Beta. true when the note was created; false when it was skipped because no contact was found (If no contact is found set to skip), and then id is empty

create_task.description: Create a task, optionally on a contact, company or deal. The due date can be given as a number of days from now (left out, the task is due today), the contact by email address or phone number, and the person it is for by their email address or as the contact's owner, so no earlier step has to look any of them up.

properties.hs_task_body: Confirm the seat count before sending.
properties.hs_task_subject: Follow up on the renewal quote

create_task.name: create_task

parameters.description: The task's title.
parameters.name: subject

parameters.description: When the task is due, such as 2026-11-20 at 9:00 AM. Beta: leave Due, Due in working days and Due in days all empty and the task is due today, at the end of the day in UTC (23:59 UTC, which is the afternoon or evening in the Americas).
parameters.name: due_at

parameters.description: Beta. Due this many working days from today, Monday to Friday: 5 created on a Wednesday is due the next Wednesday. Use it for 'kickoff call in 2 working days' instead of working the date out in an earlier step. Due wins when given. With no due field filled in, the task is due at the end of today (UTC).
parameters.name: due_in_working_days

parameters.description: Beta. Due this many days from now, weekends included: 2 created on a Friday morning is due Sunday morning. Use it for 'follow up in 2 days' instead of working the date out in an earlier step. An alternative to Due and Due in working days: Due wins when given, then Due in working days. Leave all three empty for a task due at the end of today (UTC).
parameters.name: due_in_days

parameters.description: Task notes.
parameters.name: body

parameters.description: Whether the task is already done.
parameters.name: status

parameters.description: Task priority.
parameters.name: priority

parameters.description: What kind of task this is.
parameters.name: task_type

parameters.description: The person on your team the task is for.
parameters.name: owner_id

parameters.description: Beta. The email address the person the task is for signs in to HubSpot with, such as sam@example.com, when you have their address rather than picking them above (the rep who hosted a call). When nobody in your HubSpot account has that address the task is still created, assigned to no one. Ignored when Assigned to is filled in. Leave empty to assign nobody this way.
parameters.name: owner_email

parameters.description: Beta. Give the task to the person who owns the contact it goes on (the contact chosen below, or found by email or phone), for 'a task for the contact's owner' with no step to look the owner up. When no contact is found or the contact has no owner, the task is still created and goes to Assigned to or Assigned to (by email) instead, or to no one when both are empty; assigned_to_contact_owner in the result says which happened. Leave off to use only Assigned to.
parameters.name: assign_to_contact_owner

parameters.description: Contact to attach the task to.
parameters.name: contact_id

parameters.description: Beta. Attach the task to the contact with this email address, when you have their email but not the contact. The step fails when nobody in HubSpot has it, unless If no contact is found says otherwise or Add the contact if new is on. Ignored when a contact is chosen above. Beta: it can also hold several addresses, as a list from an earlier step (a Gong call's customer_emails) or as text with commas between them, such as sam@customer.com, kim@customer.com. Then it goes on every one of them that is a HubSpot contact and the others are skipped; what happens when none of them is a contact is set by If no contact is found.
parameters.name: contact_email

parameters.description: Beta. Attach the task to the contact with this phone or mobile number, such as +1 415 555 0123, when you have a caller's number but not the contact (a missed call). Spaces, dashes and the country code don't have to match how HubSpot has it. Used when no contact is chosen above and Contact's email is empty or nobody has it. When nobody in HubSpot has the number either, If no contact is found decides what happens: by default the step fails, so set it to create the task anyway for callers who may not be contacts yet.
parameters.name: contact_phone

parameters.description: Beta. With Contact's email or Contact's phone: what to do when nobody in HubSpot has the address, any of the addresses, or the number. fail stops the workflow with an error, as it always has. skip creates no task and carries on, with created false in the result. create makes the task anyway, attached to no contact (contact_id is empty in the result), for a call or a lead that still needs following up. Leave empty for fail.
parameters.name: if_no_contact

options.label: Skip: create no task and carry on
Create the task anyway, on no contact

parameters.description: Beta. With Contact's email: when nobody in HubSpot has that address yet, add them as a contact (with only the email address) and attach the task to them instead of failing. An existing contact is left as it is. It does not apply to Contact's phone. Leave off to follow If no contact is found.
parameters.name: add_contact_if_missing

parameters.description: Company to attach the task to.
parameters.name: company_id

parameters.description: Deal to attach the task to.
parameters.name: deal_id

assigned_to_contact_owner.description: Beta. true when the task went to the contact's owner; false when Assign to the contact's owner was off, or no contact was found or it has no owner and the task went to Assigned to instead

contact_id.description: Beta. The record ID of the contact the task was put on (the first, when there are several). Empty when it was put on no contact: none was given, or none was found and If no contact is found is create or skip

contact_ids.description: Beta. The record IDs of the contacts the task was put on

contacts_found.description: Beta. How many contacts the task was put on

created.description: Beta. true when the task was created; false when it was skipped because no contact was found (If no contact is found set to skip), and then id is empty

owner_id.description: Beta. The ID of the person the task was assigned to. Empty when it was assigned to no one

found.description: True when a company in HubSpot has this domain. Use it in a condition to do one thing when the company is known and another when it isn't.

industry.description: The company's industry as HubSpot shows it, such as Computer Software. Empty when it isn't filled in.

owner_id.description: The id of the person on your team who owns the company, for an Assigned to field. Empty when nobody does.

personal_email_domain.description: True when the address is at a personal mail provider such as gmail.com, so no company was looked for.

search_deals.description: Find deals created since a date, deals that reached a stage (such as Closed won) since a date, open deals closing this month or soon, or deals nobody has touched for a while (alone or together with closing soon: 'quiet deals closing this month'). Gives each deal's owner name and email, how many match, what they're worth together and each owner's deal count and total. A message per rep still groups the deals by owner_email.
search_deals.name: search_deals

parameters.description: Only return deals created at or after this moment. Required unless you choose a stage below or fill in Not updated since, Untouched for days or Closing within days, or turn on Open deals closing this month.
parameters.name: created_after

parameters.description: Optional upper bound, exclusive. Leave empty to run the window up to now.
parameters.name: created_before

parameters.description: Beta. Turn on to get the open deals whose expected close date is in the current month, soonest first, with how many there are and what they are worth together. Needs no dates; replaces the dates below. With Untouched for days, only the deals closing this month that have also gone quiet.
parameters.name: closing_this_month

parameters.description: Beta. Only deals nobody has touched for at least this many days, longest-quiet first: 5 for 'no activity in 5 days'. Use it instead of working out a date in an earlier step. Not updated since wins when given. Turn on Open deals only to leave out deals already won or lost. It is HubSpot's last-changed date, so an edit, a note or a logged call all count as activity.
parameters.name: not_updated_for_days

parameters.description: Beta. Only open deals whose expected close date is today or within this many days, soonest first: 7 for 'closing this week'. With Untouched for days, only the deals that are both quiet and about to close, so no filter step is needed afterwards.
parameters.name: closing_in_next_days

parameters.description: Beta. Only deals created in the last this many whole days, up to but not including today: 7 on a Monday is last week, Monday to Sunday, and never counts a deal in two reports. Use it for a weekly or daily recap instead of working out the dates in earlier steps. Created after and Created before win when given.
parameters.name: created_in_last_days

parameters.description: Find deals by when they reached this stage instead of when they were created. For deals won, choose the pipeline's Closed won stage; the deal may have been created long before it was won.
parameters.name: stage

parameters.description: With a stage: only deals that reached it at or after this moment. Required when a stage is chosen, unless Reached the stage in the last days is filled in.
parameters.name: entered_stage_after

parameters.description: Beta. With a stage: only deals that reached it in the last this many whole days, up to but not including today: 7 on a Monday is last week, Monday to Sunday. Use it for a weekly or daily recap of deals won instead of working out the dates in earlier steps. Reached the stage after and before win when given.
parameters.display_name: Reached the stage in the last days
parameters.name: entered_stage_in_last_days

parameters.description: With a stage: optional upper bound, exclusive. Leave empty to run the window up to now.
parameters.name: entered_stage_before

parameters.description: Find deals nobody has touched since this moment (14 days ago for 'no activity in two weeks'), longest-quiet first. Replaces the created and stage dates above.
parameters.name: not_updated_since

parameters.description: With Not updated since: leave out deals already won or lost, which are finished rather than stuck.
parameters.name: only_open

parameters.description: How many deals to return, newest first (default 100, maximum 2000). The total count is reported in full even when more deals match than are returned.
parameters.name: limit

biggest_deal.description: The most valuable of the returned deals: name, amount_display ($8,500) and owner_name, empty when no deal has an amount. Use it for a recap's biggest deal instead of sorting the results.

by_owner.description: Each owner's number of deals and total value among the returned deals, biggest total first, with the total ready to read ($8,500). Use it for a leaderboard or a recap per rep.

amount_display.description: The amount ready to put in a message ($8,500); missing when the deal has none

url.description: Beta. A link that opens the deal in HubSpot, ready to put in a message or an email, such as https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/record/0-3/4501. Empty when HubSpot could not say which account the connection is for.

total_amount.description: What the returned deals are worth together, as a plain number for a comparison. To show it to a person, use total_amount_display.

total_amount_display.description: What the returned deals are worth together, ready to put in a message ($12,500), so a message needs no formatting step.

update_deal_stage.name: update_deal_stage

parameters.description: The deal, as an earlier step gave it, or its ID or the address of its page in HubSpot.
parameters.name: deal_id

parameters.description: The stage to move the deal to. Beta: its name as HubSpot shows it, such as Closed won or Appointment scheduled (capitals don't matter), works as well as its id. The name is looked up in the deal's own pipeline, so a Closed won in another pipeline is never picked by mistake.
parameters.name: stage

url.description: Beta. A link that opens the deal in HubSpot, ready to put in a message or an email, such as https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/record/0-3/4501. Empty when HubSpot could not say which account the connection is for.

description: Keep HubSpot up to date: create and update contacts, companies and deals, move deals through stages, and log notes and tasks.

hubspot_deal_stage_reached_trigger.description: Runs when a deal enters the stage you choose in HubSpot, such as Closed won, however long ago the deal was created. A deal that leaves the stage and comes back runs it again.

output.amount: The deal's amount, a plain number such as 50000 with no currency sign, for comparing or adding up. Blank when the deal has none.
output.amount_display: The amount written as money, such as $50,000; blank when the deal has no amount. Use it in a message rather than formatting amount.
output.closedate: When it is expected to close, or closed.
output.company_name: Beta. The name of the company the deal is with, when it has one linked in HubSpot; missing otherwise. Use it to say who a won deal is for, with no step to look the company up.
output.dealstage: The ID of the stage it is in.
output.dealtype: The deal type, such as newbusiness.
output.hubspot_owner_id: The owner's ID; empty if unassigned.
output.owner_email: The owner's email address; missing when the deal has no owner. Use it to email the owner.
output.owner_name: The owner's name as HubSpot shows it; missing when the deal has no owner. Use it in a message rather than hubspot_owner_id.

parameters.description: The deal stage to watch for, written as its name in HubSpot's standard pipeline, such as Closed won, or as its stage ID.
parameters.name: stage

hubspot_new_company_trigger.description: Runs when a company is created in HubSpot, by a person, an import, a form or another app. Companies already there when the workflow is turned on don't start it.

output.domain: Its website domain, such as example.com.
output.name: The company's name.
output.numberofemployees: How many people work there, if HubSpot has it.

hubspot_new_contact_trigger.description: Runs when a contact is created in HubSpot, by a form, an import, a person or another app.

output.hs_analytics_source: Where they came from, such as ORGANIC_SEARCH.
output.hubspot_owner_id: Beta. The owner's ID; empty if unassigned.
output.lifecyclestage: Their lifecycle stage, such as lead or customer.
output.numemployees: Beta. The number of employees at their company, if HubSpot has it, to route a lead by company size.
output.owner_email: Beta. The owner's email address; missing when the contact has no owner. Use it to email the owner, or to give them a task (Asana takes an email as the assignee).
output.owner_name: Beta. The owner's name as HubSpot shows it; missing when the contact has no owner. Use it in a message rather than hubspot_owner_id.

hubspot_new_deal_trigger.description: Runs when a deal is created in HubSpot, in any pipeline.

output.amount: The deal's amount, a plain number such as 50000 with no currency sign, for comparing or adding up. Blank when the deal has none.
output.amount_display: The amount written as money, such as $50,000; blank when the deal has no amount. Use it in a message rather than formatting amount.
output.closedate: When it is expected to close, or closed.
output.company_name: Beta. The name of the company the deal is with, when it has one linked in HubSpot; missing otherwise. Use it to say who a won deal is for, with no step to look the company up.
output.dealstage: The ID of the stage it is in.
output.dealtype: The deal type, such as newbusiness.
output.hubspot_owner_id: The owner's ID; empty if unassigned.
output.owner_email: The owner's email address; missing when the deal has no owner. Use it to email the owner.
output.owner_name: The owner's name as HubSpot shows it; missing when the deal has no owner. Use it in a message rather than hubspot_owner_id.

hubspot_new_form_submission_trigger.description: Runs when someone fills in and submits one of your HubSpot forms.

output.answers: The answers as a list of name and value pairs, in form order.
output.fields: The answers by field name, such as fields.email.
output.page_url: The page the form was submitted on.
output.submitted_at: When it was submitted, in milliseconds since 1970.

parameters.description: The form to watch. Pick it from the list, or paste the long code from the form's address in HubSpot, such as 0a1b2c3d-4e5f-6789-abcd-ef0123456789.
parameters.name: form_id

hubspot_property_changed_trigger.description: Runs when a property you choose is set or changed on a contact, company or deal in HubSpot, such as a contact's lifecycle stage, or only when it changes to the value you give, such as customer.

output.changed_property: The property that changed, such as lifecyclestage.
output.createdate: When the record was created. The record's other details come by property name too, such as email for a contact or dealname for a deal, as New contact, New company and New deal give them.
output.id: The record ID of the contact, company or deal that changed.
output.new_value: Its new value, as HubSpot stores it, such as customer.
output.previous_value: Its value before the change; empty if it had none.

parameters.description: Whether to watch contacts, companies or deals.
parameters.name: object_type

parameters.description: The property to watch, such as Lifecycle stage.
parameters.name: property

parameters.description: Only run when the property changes to this value, as HubSpot stores it, such as customer. Leave blank to run for every change.
parameters.name: value
